inputs.name: Cohomology and rationality of regular algebraic cuspidal GLn representations
inputs.author: Laurent Clozel
inputs.title: Motifs et formes automorphes: applications du principe de fonctorialite (1990)
inputs.accepted_statement: Regular C-algebraic cuspidal representations are cohomological for the matching algebraic coefficient; their finite parts have number-field models and Aut(C) conjugates remain cuspidal with permuted infinity type.
inputs.exact_specialization: Only GL4 over fixed imaginary quadratic K, with parallel infOf(e+1,e,1,0). CX1 constructs the actual highest weight (-3,-3,-e-1,-e-1) and a polynomial rank bound. CX2 explicitly treats the algebraic Satake normalization and polarized subset.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

checked_primary_author_restatements.locator: Lemma 2.12 and Proposition 2.15 (cohomological and rationality specialization)

inputs.scope_guard: No L-algebraic substitution for the C-algebraic theorem; the integer power q^{j(j-1)/2} in CX.10 removes the square-root normalization ambiguity.

inputs.name: Finite arithmetic CW model
inputs.author: Armand Borel and Jean-Pierre Serre
inputs.title: Corners and arithmetic groups, Comment. Math. Helv. 48 (1973), 436--491
inputs.accepted_statement: A torsion-free arithmetic quotient, with the rational split central direction removed, admits the compact Borel--Serre manifold-with-corners model and hence finite CW type.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX1 uses only finitely many level-three components for each fixed imaginary quadratic field. It proves torsion-freeness and the covering index <=(3L)^32, then counts lifted cells. No uniform family theorem is assumed.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Cuspidal cohomology injects ordinary cohomology
inputs.author: Armand Borel, Jean-Pierre Labesse and Joachim Schwermer
inputs.title: On the cuspidal cohomology of S-arithmetic subgroups of reductive groups over number fields, Compositio 102 (1996), 1--40
inputs.theorem_reference: Theorem 5.2, arithmetic case; following remark identifies the cuspidal direct summand
inputs.accepted_statement: Cuspidal relative Lie algebra cohomology is a direct summand of arithmetic cohomology with the same finite-dimensional algebraic coefficient.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX1 applies to GL4/K at principal level3L and its same coefficient E_e. Distinct cusp classes yield distinct nonzero summands; their number is bounded by all ordinary cohomology dimensions.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Polarized automorphic Galois representations, local-global compatibility, Hodge numbers and purity
inputs.author: Thomas Barnet-Lamb, Toby Gee, David Geraghty and Richard Taylor
inputs.title: Potential automorphy and change of weight, Annals of Mathematics 179 (2014), 501--609
inputs.accepted_statement: For regular algebraic cuspidal polarized pairs over CM fields and every coefficient prime, the semisimple Galois representation exists; full Frobenius-semisimplified compatibility and purity hold away the coefficient prime; de Rham Hodge numbers are lambda_i+n-i; spherical places above that prime give crystalline representations.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX4 first constructs the actual polarized pair and corrects its sign, then identifies the original irreducible restriction by Chebotarev. CX3 uses every coefficient prime, including2 for non-p valuations, and the coefficient prime p for integrality. Hodge numbers are(0,-1,-e,-e-1); geometric weight is -e-1; arithmetic roots are their inverses.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Semisimplified local-global compatibility at the coefficient prime
inputs.author: Thomas Barnet-Lamb, Toby Gee, David Geraghty and Richard Taylor
inputs.title: Local-global compatibility for l=p, II, Ann. Sci. ENS 47 (2014), 165--179
inputs.accepted_statement: At every place over l, the semisimplified Weil--Deligne representation of a regular algebraic essentially conjugate-self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation matches rec(pi_v |det|^{(1-n)/2}) up to semisimplification.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX5 uses only equality of semisimple Weil representations. The possibly unmatched nilpotent operator is bounded by rankN<=3. No Shin-regularity or full monodromy comparison at l is inferred.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Finite-coefficient p-adic Hodge exactness and weak admissibility
inputs.author: Jean-Marc Fontaine; Pierre Colmez and Jean-Marc Fontaine; Laurent Berger
inputs.title: Construction des representations p-adiques semi-stables (2000), with classical de Rham monodromy theorem
inputs.theorem_reference: Proposition4.2 and corollary to Theorem4.3; Berger, Representations p-adiques et equations differentielles, Theorems0.6 and5.19 (arXiv v3)
inputs.accepted_statement: The potentially semistable comparison functor is exact on its category; de Rham representations of finite p-adic local fields are potentially semistable; crystalline modules are weakly admissible with the corresponding filtration and tensor, dual and scalar-extension compatibilities.
inputs.exact_specialization: Only finite common coefficient fields after the proved Baire capture. CX4 does not assume arbitrary extensions of de Rham characters are de Rham. CX5 applies exactness after identification with an automorphic de Rham representation. CX3 derives slopes in[-e-1,0] from the subobject and quotient inequalities, so inverse geometric Frobenius roots are integral.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Local Langlands conductor compatibility
inputs.author: Michael Harris and Richard Taylor; Guy Henniart; Peter Scholze
inputs.title: The local Langlands correspondence for GLn over p-adic fields, Inventiones192 (2013), 663--715
inputs.theorem_reference: Theorem14.1 (epsilon-factor compatibility), with the standard extension from supercuspidals to Weil--Deligne parameters
inputs.accepted_statement: The GLn correspondence preserves local L and epsilon factors, hence Artin conductor exponents; it is compatible with characters, unramified twists and spherical parameters.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX5 only uses conductor and spherical compatibility. Its elementary formula a(rho,N)=a(rho)+dimV^I-dim(kerN)^I bounds monodromy loss by3, and unramified normalization does not change conductors.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Generic local newvectors
inputs.author: Herve Jacquet, Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro and Joseph Shalika
inputs.title: Conducteur des representations du groupe lineaire, Math. Ann.256 (1981), 199--214
inputs.accepted_statement: An irreducible generic representation of GLn over a nonarchimedean local field has nonzero K1(p^a)-fixed vectors at its conductor exponent a, and a=0 is the spherical case.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX5 takes the smaller principal subgroup modulo p^{7v(M)} and tensors local vectors. The original target Galois level M is never replaced by M^7.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Finite local/global reciprocity and norm compatibility
inputs.author: J. S. Milne
inputs.title: Class Field Theory, version4.03 (2020)
inputs.theorem_reference: ChapterI, Theorem1.1 and norm functoriality; ChapterIII section3; ChapterV section5
inputs.accepted_statement: Finite abelian characters correspond to finite Hecke characters, local reciprocity is compatible with norms and the cyclotomic action, and a quadratic character kills norms from its quadratic extension.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX4 explicitly constructs chi from theta*cyclo^3 and sign-corrects by eta_K, preserving equality only on G_K. CX5 proves the needed norm congruence by a determinant in an integral local basis.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Strong multiplicity one and genericity for cuspidal GLn
inputs.author: Jacquet, Piatetski-Shapiro and Shalika; James W. Cogdell
inputs.title: Lectures on L-functions, converse theorems, and functoriality for GLn (2004)
inputs.theorem_reference: Theorem4.3 (strong multiplicity one); Corollary4.1.2 (global and local genericity of cuspidal representations)
inputs.accepted_statement: Cuspidal GLn representations agreeing at almost all finite places are globally isomorphic; each local component is generic.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX1 counts distinct global cusp labels, CX2 transports polarization, CX4 constructs the actual polarization by comparing Satake parameters, and CX5 invokes local newvectors only for genuine cusp components.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.

inputs.name: Finite arithmetic of quadratic fields, class groups and Chebotarev
inputs.author: J. S. Milne
inputs.title: Algebraic Number Theory, version3.08 (2020)
inputs.theorem_reference: Quadratic integer-basis/discriminant calculation; finite ideal class group; Theorem8.31 (Chebotarev)
inputs.accepted_statement: Quadratic fields have the usual integral bases and discriminants; number-field class groups are finite; Frobenius conjugacy classes outside any finite set are dense in finite Galois quotients.
inputs.exact_specialization: CX6 constructs eighteen fields with pairwise prime discriminants by an elementary Euclidean argument. CX1 uses class-group finiteness for one fixed adelic quotient. CX4 passes cofinite Frobenius equality to continuous traces and proves the ensuing semisimple character comparison.
inputs.status: Accepted named classical theorem; actual specialization and joins proved in CX.
